newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan airlines ask for permission to raise fares.
newsitem.headline: Japan airlines ask for permission to raise fares.

text.p: Japan's major international air carriers said on Wednesday that they have asked the Ministry of Transportation for permission to raise international airfares by three percent, beginning on December 15.
The companies are Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL), All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) and Japan Air System Co Ltd.
If approved, the standard price for a round-trip economy-class ticket for flights between Tokyo and Los Angeles, for example, would rise to 353,100 yen from 342,800 yen.
The Japanese airlines hopes to raise airfares for a combined total of 127 international routes.
The proposed airfare increase is based on a November 15 agreement at the International Air Transport Association (IATA), an industry organisation based in Geneva.
IATA members have agreed to increase fares in the hope of passing on the recent rise in fuel costs to passengers.

ANA said last month when it announced its earnings for the half year to September 30 that the cost of fuel in the six-month period rose nine percent year-on-year. It also expects fuel costs for the full year to March 31 will increase by 10 biilion yen from the previous year.

"The proposed rate hike would be a plus for the airlines' earnings," said Tadatoshi Utaka, an analyst at Nikko Research Centre. He said that demand for air travel would not be affected even if airfares were to be raised.

Meanwhile, Masanori Maruo, an analyst at Daiwa Research Institute, said that the impact of a fare increase on earnings would be very limited as the planned hike would apply only to standard rates and not to discounted rates such as those for packaged tours.
